			<font style="display: inline;font-size:12pt;">First Capital Bancorp, Inc.</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:12pt;">, (the Company)</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:12pt;"> is a bank holding company that was incorporated under Virginia law in 2006.&nbsp;&nbsp;Pursuant to a statutory share exchange </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:12pt;">in</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:12pt;"> September 2006, we became a bank holding company.&nbsp;&nbsp;We conduct our primary operations through our wholly owned subsidiary, First Capital Bank</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:12pt;"> (the Bank)</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:12pt;">, which is chartered under Virginia law</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:12pt;"> and opened for business in 1998</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:12pt;">.&nbsp;&nbsp;We have one other wholly owned subsidiary, FCRV Statutory Trust 1, which is a Delaware Business Trust that we formed in connection with the issuance of tru</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:12pt;">st preferred capital notes in </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:12pt;">2006.</font>

			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:12pt;">We offer a full range of deposit services that are typically available in most banks including checking accounts, NOW accounts, savings accounts</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:12pt;">,</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:12pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:12pt;">money </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:12pt;">market accounts</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:12pt;">,</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:12pt;"> certificates of deposit</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:12pt;">, and individual retirement accounts</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:12pt;">.&nbsp; </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:12pt;">All deposit services are tailored to our market </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:12pt;">area at </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:12pt;">competitive rates</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:12pt;">.&nbsp; </font>

institutions.&nbsp; </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:12pt;">However, w</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:12pt;">e believe that there is a large customer base in our market area that </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:12pt;">relies on word-of-mouth advertising and </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:12pt;">prefers d</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:12pt;">oing business with local organizations, but which also wants convenient banking</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:12pt;">.&nbsp;&nbsp;We seek to fill th</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:12pt;">ese</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:12pt;"> need</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New and work</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:12pt;">, associating with a shared network of ATMs, and expanding our mobile and online banking services</font><font support a substantially larger banking institution without incurring meaningful additional expenses. </font>

			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:12pt;">We compete with other commercial banks, savings and loan associations, credit unions, consumer finance companies, securities brokerage firms, insurance companies, money market mutual funds and other financial institutions operating in the Richmond metropolitan area and elsewhere.&nbsp;&nbsp;Many of our non-bank competitors are not subject to the same extensive federal regulations that govern federally-insured banks and state regulations governing state chartered banks.&nbsp;&nbsp;As a result, such non-bank competitors may have certain advantages over us in providing certain services.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Arial;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:12pt;">&nbsp;</font>

			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:12pt;">Our primary market area is a highly competitive, highly branched banking market.&nbsp;&nbsp;Competition in the market area for loans to small and medium-sized businesses and professionals is intense, and pricing is important.&nbsp;&nbsp;Many of our competitors have substantially greater reso</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:12pt;">urces and lending limits than we do</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:12pt;"> and offer certain services, such as extensive and established branch networks, that we are not currently providing.&nbsp;&nbsp;Moreover, larger institutions operating in the Richmond metropolitan area have access to borrowed funds at lower cost than the funds that are presently available to us.&nbsp;&nbsp;Deposit competition among institutions in the market area also is strong.&nbsp;&nbsp;Competition for depositors&#x2019; funds comes from U.S. Government securities, private issuers of debt obligations and suppliers of other investment alternatives for depositors, among other sources.</font>

			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:12pt;">At June 30, 2014, the latest date such information is available from the FDIC, the Bank&#x2019;s deposit market share was 0.73% in the City of Richmond, 1.45% in Chesterfield County, 3.13% in Hanover County, and 0.37% in Henrico County.</font>

		<p style="margin:0pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Arial;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:bold;font-size:12pt;">Governmental Monetary Policies</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Arial;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:12pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Arial;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:12pt;">Our earnings and growth are affected not only by general economic conditions, but also by the monetary policies of various governmental regulatory authorities, particularly the Federal Re</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:12pt;">serve Bank (FRB</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:12pt;">).&nbsp;&nbsp;The FRB implements national monetary policy by its open market operations in United States Government securities, control of the discount rate and establishment of reserve requirements against both member and nonmember financial institutions&#x2019; deposits.&nbsp;&nbsp;These actions have a significant effect on the overall growth and distribution of loans, investments and deposits, as well as the rates earned on loans, or paid on deposits.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Arial;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:12pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Arial;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:12pt;">Our management is unable to predict the effect of possible changes in monetary policies upon our future operating results.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-size:12pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">Lending Activities</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">Credit Policies</font><font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The principal risk associated with each of the categories of loans in our portfolio is the creditworthiness of our borrowers.&nbsp;&nbsp;Within each category, such risk is increased or decreased, depending on various factors.&nbsp;&nbsp;The risks associated with real estate mortgage loans, commercial loans and consumer loans vary based on employment levels, consumer confidence, fluctuations in the value of real estate and other conditions that affect the ability of borrowers to repay indebtedness.&nbsp;&nbsp;The risk associated with real estate construction loans varies based on the supply and demand for the type of real estate under construction.&nbsp;&nbsp;In an effort to manage these risks, we have loan approval limits for individual loan officers based on their position and level of experience. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">We have written policies and procedures to help manage credit risk.&nbsp;&nbsp;We use a loan review process that includes a portfolio management strategy, guidelines for underwriting standards and risk assessment, procedures for ongoing identification and management of credit </font><font style="display: inline;">problems</font><font style="display: inline;">, and annual independent third party portfolio reviews to establish loss exposure and to monitor compliance with policies.&nbsp;&nbsp;Our loan approval process include</font><font style="display: inline;">s our Management Loan Committee and</font><font style="display: inline;"> the Loan Committee of the Board of Directors</font><font style="display: inline;">.&nbsp;&nbsp;Our </font><font style="display: inline;">Chief Credit Officer is responsible for reporting </font><font style="display: inline;">monthly </font><font style="display: inline;">to the </font><font style="display: inline;">Board of </font><font style="display: inline;">Directors on the activities of the Management Loan Committee and on the status of various delinquent and non-performing loans.&nbsp;&nbsp;The </font><font style="display: inline;">Board of Directors</font><font style="display: inline;"> reviews lending policies </font><font style="display: inline;">and recommends guidelines for the Bank&#x2019;s appetite for specific types of loans as a percentage of the Bank&#x2019;s total risk-based capital.</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">Loan Originations </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Real estate loan originations come primarily through direct solicitations by our loan officers, continued business from current customers, and through referrals. C</font><font style="display: inline;">onstruction loans are obtained through direct</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">solicitations by</font><font style="display: inline;"> our construction loan officers and continued business from current customers.&nbsp;&nbsp;Commercial real estate loan originations are obtained through broker referrals, direct solicitation by our loan officers and continued business from current customers.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">

		</p>
		<p><font size="1"> </font></p><div style="width:100%">

		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:center;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 11pt">

			<font style="display: inline;">6</font>

		</p>

		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 11pt">

			&nbsp;

		</p>

</div><hr size="3" style="color:#999999" width="100%" align="center"></hr><p style="page-break-after:always">&nbsp;</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;;font-size: 12pt"><font style="display: inline;"></font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Our loan officers, as part of the application process, review all loan applications.&nbsp;&nbsp;Information is obtained concerning the income, financial condition, employment and credit history of the applicant.&nbsp;&nbsp;If commercial real estate is involved, information is also obtained concerning cash flow available for debt service.&nbsp;&nbsp;Loan quality is analyzed based on our experience and credit underwriting guidelines.&nbsp;&nbsp;Income producing real estate collateral for loan</font><font style="display: inline;">s in excess of $250 thousand is</font><font style="display: inline;"> appraised by independent appraisers who have been pre-approved by meeting the requirement of providing a current and valid license certification and based on the lender&#x2019;s experience with these appraisers.&nbsp;&nbsp;Evaluations for real estate collateral for loans less than $250 thousand are made by the loan officer</font><font style="display: inline;">s</font><font style="display: inline;">.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">In the normal course of business, we make various commitments and incur certain contingent liabilities that are disclosed but not reflected in our annual financial statements</font><font style="display: inline;">,</font><font style="display: inline;"> including commitments to extend credit. At December 31, 201</font><font style="display: inline;">4</font><font style="display: inline;">, &nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">our </font><font style="display: inline;">commitments to extend credit totaled $</font><font style="display: inline;">38.8</font><font style="display: inline;"> million. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">Construction Lending </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">We make local construction and land acquisition and development loans. Residential houses and commercial real estate under construction and the underlying land secure </font><font style="display: inline;">these </font><font style="display: inline;">construction loans.&nbsp;&nbsp;At December 31, 201</font><font style="display: inline;">4</font><font style="display: inline;">, construction, land acquisition and land development loans outstanding were $</font><font style="display: inline;">85.1</font><font style="display: inline;"> million, or 1</font><font style="display: inline;">7.67</font><font style="display: inline;">% of total loans.&nbsp;&nbsp;These loans are c</font><font style="display: inline;">oncentrated in our local market</font><font style="display: inline;">.&nbsp;&nbsp;Because the interest rate charged on these loans usually floats with the market, these loans assist us in managing our interest rate risk.&nbsp;&nbsp;Construction lending entails significant additional risks, compared to residential mortgage lending.&nbsp;&nbsp;Construction loans often involve larger loan balances concentrated with single borrowers or groups of related borrowers.&nbsp;&nbsp;In addition, the value of the building under construction is only estimable when the loan funds are disbursed.&nbsp;&nbsp;Thus, it is more difficult to evaluate accurately the total loan funds required to complete a project and related loan-to-value ratios.&nbsp;&nbsp;To mitigate the risks associated with construction lending, we generally limit loan amounts to 80% of appraised value in addition to analyzing the creditworthiness of the borrower.&nbsp;&nbsp;We also obtain a first lien on the property as security for construction loans and typically require personal guarantees from the borrower&#x2019;s principal owners. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">Commercial Business Loans </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Commercial business loans generally have a higher degree of risk than </font><font style="display: inline;">loans secured by real property, although they</font><font style="display: inline;"> have higher yields.&nbsp;&nbsp;To manage these risks, we </font><font style="display: inline;">typically</font><font style="display: inline;"> obtain appropriate collateral and persona</font><font style="display: inline;">l guarantees from the borrower&#x2019;s</font><font style="display: inline;"> principal owner</font><font style="display: inline;">s</font><font style="display: inline;"> and monitor the fina</font><font style="display: inline;">ncial condition of the related business</font><font style="display: inline;">.&nbsp;&nbsp;Residential mortgage loans generally are made on the basis of the borrower&#x2019;s ability to make repayment from employment and other income and are secured by real estate whose value tends to be readily ascertainable.&nbsp;&nbsp;In contrast, commercial business loans typically are made on the basis of the borrower&#x2019;s ability to make repayment from </font><font style="display: inline;">the related</font><font style="display: inline;"> business</font><font style="display: inline;">&#x2019; cash flow</font><font style="display: inline;"> and are secured by business assets, such as commercial real estate, accounts receivable, equipment and inventory.&nbsp;&nbsp;As a result, the availability of funds for the repayment of commercial business loans is substantially dependent on the success of the business itself.&nbsp;&nbsp;Furthermore, the collateral for commercial business loans may depreciate over time and generally cannot be appraised with as much precision as residential real estate.&nbsp;&nbsp;We have a loan review and monitoring process to regularly assess the repayment ability of commercial borrowers.&nbsp;&nbsp;At December 31, 201</font><font style="display: inline;">4</font><font style="display: inline;">, commercial loans totaled $</font><font style="display: inline;">66.9</font><font style="display: inline;"> million, or </font><font style="display: inline;">13.88% of total loans</font><font style="display: inline;">. &nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">

		</p>
		<p><font size="1"> </font></p><div style="width:100%">

		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:center;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 11pt">

			<font style="display: inline;">7</font>

		</p>

		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 11pt">

			&nbsp;

		</p>

</div><hr size="3" style="color:#999999" width="100%" align="center"></hr><p style="page-break-after:always">&nbsp;</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;;font-size: 12pt"><font style="display: inline;"></font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">Commercial Real Estate Lending </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Commercial real estate loans are secured by various types of commercial real estate in our market area</font><font style="display: inline;">,</font><font style="display: inline;"> including commercial buildings and offices, recreational facilities, small shopping centers, churches and hotels.&nbsp;&nbsp;At December 31, 201</font><font style="display: inline;">4</font><font style="display: inline;">, commercial real estate loans totaled $</font><font style="display: inline;">182.7 million, or 37.92% of</font><font style="display: inline;"> total loans.&nbsp;&nbsp;We may lend up to 80% of the secured property&#x2019;s appraised value.&nbsp;&nbsp;Commercial real estate loans typically involve larger loan balances concentrated with single borrowers or groups of related borrowers.&nbsp;&nbsp;Additionally, the payment experience on loans secured by income producing properties is typically dependent on the successful operation of a business or a real estate project and thus may be subject, to a greater extent, to adverse conditions in the real estate market or in the economic environment.&nbsp;&nbsp;Our commercial real estate loan underwriting criteria requires an examination of debt service coverage ratios, the borrower&#x2019;s creditworthiness and prior credit history and reputation, and we typically require personal guarantees or endorsements of the borrower</font><font style="display: inline;">&#x2019;</font><font style="display: inline;">s principal owners.&nbsp;&nbsp;In addition, we carefully evaluate the location of the security property. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">Residential Real Estate Lending</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Residential real estate loans at December 31, 201</font><font style="display: inline;">4</font><font style="display: inline;">, accounted for $</font><font style="display: inline;">145.2</font><font style="display: inline;"> million, or 3</font><font style="display: inline;">0.14% of total loans</font><font style="display: inline;">.&nbsp;&nbsp;Residential first mortgage loans represent $8</font><font style="display: inline;">4.1</font><font style="display: inline;"> million or </font><font style="display: inline;">57.92</font><font style="display: inline;">% of total residential real estate loans and are primarily made up of investor loans to qualified borrowers leasing property.&nbsp; </font><font style="display: inline;">As of December 31, 2014, m</font><font style="display: inline;">ultifamily and home equity loans represent $</font><font style="display: inline;">37.2</font><font style="display: inline;"> million and $</font><font style="display: inline;">20.5</font><font style="display: inline;"> million, respectively, and junior liens account for $</font><font style="display: inline;">3.2</font><font style="display: inline;"> million of total residential real estate loans.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">All residential mortgage loans originated by us contain a &#x201C;due-on-sale&#x201D; clause providing that we may declare the unpaid principal balance due and payable upon sale or transfer of the mortgaged premises.&nbsp;&nbsp;In connection with residential real estate loans, we require title insurance, hazard insurance and</font><font style="display: inline;">,</font><font style="display: inline;"> if appropriate, flood insurance.&nbsp;&nbsp;We do not require escrows for real estate taxes and insurance. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">Consumer Lending </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">We offer various secured and unsecured consumer loans, including unsecured personal loans and lines of credit, automobile loans, boat loans, deposit account loans, installment and demand loans and credit cards.&nbsp;&nbsp;At December 31, 201</font><font style="display: inline;">4</font><font style="display: inline;">, we had consumer loans of $</font><font style="display: inline;">1.9</font><font style="display: inline;"> million or 0.</font><font style="display: inline;">39</font><font style="display: inline;">% of total loans. Such loans are generally made to customers with whom we have a pre-existing relationship.&nbsp;&nbsp;We currently originate all of our consumer loans in our</font><font style="display: inline;"> local</font><font style="display: inline;"> market area. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Consumer loans may entail greater risk than residential mortgage loans, particularly in the case of consumer loans that are un</font><font style="display: inline;">der-</font><font style="display: inline;">secured, such as loans secured by rapidly depreciable assets </font><font style="display: inline;">like</font><font style="display: inline;"> automobiles.&nbsp;&nbsp;Any repossessed collateral for a defaulted consumer loan may not provide an adequate source of repayment as a result of the greater likelihood of damage, loss or depreciation. Due to the relatively small amounts involved, any remaining deficiency often does not warrant further substantial collection efforts against the borrower.&nbsp;&nbsp;In addition, consumer loan collections are dependent on the borrower&#x2019;s continuing financial stability, and thus are more likely to be adversely affected by job loss, divorce, illness or personal bankruptcy. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">

		</p>
		<p><font size="1"> </font></p><div style="width:100%">

			<font style="display: inline;">8</font>

		</p>

		</p>

		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Arial;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:12pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Arial;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:12pt;">The underwriting standards we employ to mitigate the risk for consumer loans include a determination of the applicant&#x2019;s payment history on other </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:12pt;">debts and an assessment of the applicant&#x2019;s</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:12pt;"> ability to meet existing obligations and payments on the proposed loan.&nbsp;&nbsp;The stability of the applicant&#x2019;s monthly income may be determined by verification of gross monthly income from primary employment and from any verifiable secondary income.&nbsp;&nbsp;Although creditworthiness of the applicant is of primary consideration, the underwriting process also includes an analysis of the value of the security in relation to the proposed loan amount.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 0.7pt;text-indent:35.3pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Calibri;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:bold;font-size:12pt;">&nbsp;</font>

		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-size:12pt;">SUPERVISION AND REGULATION</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:24.5pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">General</font><font style="display: inline;">.</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;"> As a bank holding company, the Company is subject to regulation under the Bank Holding Company Act of 1956, as amended, and the examination and reporting requirements of the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System. As a state-chartered commercial bank, the Bank is subject to regulation, supervision and examination by the Virginia State Corporation Commission&#x2019;s Bureau of Financial Institutions. It is also subject to regulation, supervision and examination by the Federal Reserve Board. Other federal and state laws, including various consumer and compliance laws, govern the activities of the Bank, the investments that it makes and the aggregate amount of loans that it may grant to one borrower.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;text-indent:24.5pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>

			<font style="display: inline;">The following sections summarize the significant federal and state laws applicable to the Company and its subsidiaries. To the extent that statutory or regulatory provisions are described, the description is qualified in its entirety by reference to that particular statutory or regulatory provision. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;text-indent:24.5pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">

			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">The Bank Holding Company Act</font><font style="display: inline;">. &nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">Under the Bank Holding Company Act, the Company is subject to periodic examination by the Federal Reserve and is required to file periodic reports regarding its operations and any additional information that the Federal Reserve may require. Activities at the bank holding company level are limited to the following: </font>

</div><hr size="3" style="color:#999999" width="100%" align="center"></hr><p style="page-break-after:always">&nbsp;</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:24.5pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;;font-size: 12pt"><font style="display: inline;">In addition, and subject to some exceptions, the Bank Holding Company Act and the Change in Bank Control Act, together with their</font><font style="display: inline;"> respective</font><font style="display: inline;"> regulations, require</font><font style="display: inline;">s</font><font style="display: inline;"> Federal Reserve approval prior to any person or company</font><font style="display: inline;"> acquiring</font><font style="display: inline;"> 25% or more of any class of voting securities of the bank holding company. Prior notice to the Federal Reserve is required if a person acquires 10% or more, but less than 25%, of any class of voting securities of a bank or bank holding company and either has registered securities under Section&nbsp;12 of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 or no other person owns a greater percentage of that class of voting securities immediately after the transaction.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:24.5pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:24.5pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The Gramm-Leach-Bliley Act of 1999 (GLBA</font><font style="display: inline;">) made substantial revisions to the statutory restrictions separating banking activities from other financial activities. Under the GLBA, bank holding companies that are well-capitalized and well-managed and meet other conditions can elect to become &#x201C;financial holding companies.&#x201D; As financial holding companies, they and their subsidiaries are permitted to acquire or engage in previously impermissible activities such as insurance underwriting, securities underwriting and distribution, travel agency activities, insurance agency activities, merchant banking and other activities that the Federal Reserve determines to be financial in nature or complementary to these activities. Financial holding companies continue to be subject to the overall oversight and supervision of the Federal Reserve, but the GLBA applies the concept of functional regulation to the activities conducted by subsidiaries</font><font style="display: inline;"> of financial holding companies</font><font style="display: inline;">. For example, insurance activities would be subject to supervision and regulation by state insurance authorities. Although the Company has not elected to become a financial holding company in order to exercise the broader activity powers provided by the GLBA, the Company may elect do so in the future. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;text-indent:24.5pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:24.5pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">Payment of Dividends</font><font style="display: inline;">. &nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">The Company is a legal entity separate and distinct from the Bank.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Bank is subject to laws and regulations that limit the amount of dividends it can pay. In addition, both the Company and the Bank are subject to various regulatory restrictions relating to the payment of dividends, including requirements to maintain capital at or above regulatory minimums. Banking regulators have indicated that banking organizations should generally pay dividends only if the organization&#x2019;s current earnings are sufficient to fully fund the dividends and the prospective rate of earnings retention appears consistent with the organization&#x2019;s capital needs, asset quality and overall financial condition.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Bank paid no divi</font><font style="display: inline;">dends to the Company during 2014</font><font style="display: inline;"> and 201</font><font style="display: inline;">3</font><font style="display: inline;">.</font><font style="display: inline;"> &nbsp;In December 2014, the Company&#x2019;s board of directors approved an annual cash dividend policy.&nbsp;&nbsp;No dividends have yet been declared or paid in connection with such dividend policy.</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;text-indent:24.5pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:24.5pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The </font><font style="display: inline;">Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation (</font><font style="display: inline;">FDIC</font><font style="display: inline;">)</font><font style="display: inline;"> has the general authority to limit the dividends paid by insured banks if the payment is deemed an unsafe and unsound practice. The FDIC has indicated that paying dividends that deplete a bank&#x2019;s capital base to an inadequate level would be an unsound and unsafe banking practice. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;text-indent:24.5pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:24.5pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">Insurance of Accounts, Assessments and Regulation by the FDIC</font><font style="display: inline;">.</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;"> The Bank&#x2019;s deposits are insured </font><font style="display: inline;">by the FDIC up to</font><font style="display: inline;"> limits </font><font style="display: inline;">set forth under applicable law, which are currently $250 thousand.</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">The FDIC has a risk-based assessment system, under which insured institutions are assigned to one of four risk categories based on supervisory evaluations, regulatory capital levels, and certain other factors.&nbsp;&nbsp;The assessment base is an institution&#x2019;s average consolidated assets less average tangible equity, and the initial base assessment rates are between 5 and 35 basis points, depending on the institution&#x2019;s risk category, and subject to potential adjustment based on certain long-term unsecured debt and brokered deposits held by the institution</font><font style="display: inline;">.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">

		</p>
		<p><font size="1"> </font></p><div style="width:100%">

		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:center;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 11pt">

			<font style="display: inline;">10</font>

		</p>

		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 11pt">

			&nbsp;

		</p>

</div><hr size="3" style="color:#999999" width="100%" align="center"></hr><p style="page-break-after:always">&nbsp;</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;;font-size: 12pt"><font style="display: inline;"></font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;text-indent:24.5pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:24.5pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">Capital Requirements</font><font style="display: inline;">.</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;"> The Federal Reserve Board has issued risk-based and leverage capital guidelines applicable to banking organizations that it supervises. Under the risk-based capital requirements, the Company and the Bank are each generally required to maintain a minimum ratio of total capital to risk-weighted assets of 8%. At least half of the total capital must be composed of &#x201C;Tier 1 Capital&#x201D;, which is defined as common equity, retained earnings and qualifying perpetual preferred stock, less certain intangibles. The remainder may consist of &#x201C;Tier 2 Capital&#x201D;, which is defined as specific subordinated debt, some hybrid capital instruments and other qualifying preferred stock and a limited amount of the loan loss allowance. In addition, each of the federal banking regulatory agencies has established minimum leverage capital requirements for banking organizations. Under these requirements, banking organizations must maintain a minimum ratio of Tier 1 capital to adjusted average quarterly assets equal to 3% to 5%, subject to federal bank regulatory evaluation of an organization&#x2019;s overall safety and soundness. In sum, the capital measures used by the federal banking regulators are as follows: </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>

					<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;height:1.00pt;overflow:hidden;font-size:0pt;">
						<font style="display: inline;font-size:1pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
				</td>
				<td valign="top" style="width:02.00%;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-left:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-right:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;height:1.00pt;padding:0pt;">
					<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;height:1.00pt;overflow:hidden;font-size:0pt;">
						&nbsp;</p>

						&nbsp;</p>
