</div><hr size="3" style="color:#999999" width="100%" align="center"></hr><p style="page-break-after:always">&nbsp;</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;;font-size: 11pt"><font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;font-size:11pt;"></font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 11pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;font-size:11pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 11pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;font-size:11pt;">Year ended December 31, 2014 compared to year ended December 31, 2013</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 11pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:11pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 11pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:11pt;">The low interest rates during the last year have placed downward pressure on the Company&#x2019;s yield on earning assets and related interest income.&nbsp;&nbsp;The decline in earning asset yields, however, has been offset principally by repricing of money market accounts and certificates of deposit to lower yields.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company also expects continued pressure on net interest margin from low rates over the next several quarters.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 11pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:11pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 11pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:11pt;">Net interest income for the year ended December 31, 2014 increased 7.87% to $19.4 million compared to $18.0 million for the year ended December 31, 2013, due primarily to an increase in loan interest income to $22.8 million in 2014 compared to $20.9 million in 2013. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 11pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:11pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 11pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:11pt;">Average total earning assets increased $43.0 million, or 8.44%, to $552.5 million for 2014 compared to $509.5 million for 2013.&nbsp;&nbsp;Average loans, net of unearned income, increased $46.9 million during 2014 to $456.1 million.&nbsp;&nbsp;The average rate earned on net loans decreased 12 basis points during 2014 to 4.99% from 5.11% for the year ended December 31, 2013, reflecting the competitive rate environment.&nbsp;&nbsp;Average investment securities decreased $5.3 million from $83.3 million at December 31, 2013 to $77.9 million at December 31, 2014, reflecting cash flow needs to fund loan growth.&nbsp;&nbsp;The average yield in our securities portfolio decreased 43 basis points during 2014 to 2.30% compared to 2.73% during 2013, reflecting the restructuring of the investment portfolio to reduce its duration and volatility.&nbsp;&nbsp;Income on interest bearing deposit assets increased from $21 thousand for 2013 to $34 thousand for 2014 as the average balance increased from $7.6 million during 2013 compared to $8.8 million during 2014, reflecting the purchase of certificates of deposit from other banks in conjunction with the restructuring of the investment portfolio.&nbsp;&nbsp;Based on all the factors described herein, the yield on total average earning assets decreased 11 basis points to 4.54% for 2014 from 4.65% for 2013.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 11pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:11pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 11pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:11pt;">Average interest bearing deposit liabilities increased $12.7 million or 3.27% to $399.9 million during 2014 from $387.3 million during 2013.&nbsp;&nbsp;Interest expense on deposit liabilities decreased $441 thousand for 2014 compared to 2013.&nbsp;&nbsp;The average cost of interest-bearing deposits decreased 15 basis points from 1.21% for 2013 to 1.06% for 2014, reflecting the repricing of money market accounts and certificates of deposit to lower yields.&nbsp;&nbsp;The cost of certificates of deposit decreased 21 basis points from 1.80% for 2013 to 1.59% for 2014.&nbsp;&nbsp;The average balance in money market deposit accounts increased $8.1 million during 2014 compared to 2013, and the related cost decreased from 0.42% for 2013 to 0.40% for 2014.&nbsp; </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:11pt;">We expect deposit costs</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:11pt;"> to continue to decrease in 2015</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:11pt;"> as certificates of deposit reprice and the rate on money market accounts decreases, but to a lesser extent than such costs decreased </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:11pt;">2014. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 11pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:11pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 11pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:11pt;">Average Federal Home Loan Bank (FHLB) advances increased $11.9 million from $26.9 million at December 31, 2013 to $38.8 million at December 31, 2014, while the average rate on such advances decreased from 1.23% in 2013 to 1.16% for 2014 due to </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:11pt;">the </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:11pt;">lower interest rates on new advances</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:11pt;">.&nbsp; </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:11pt;">FHLB advances were used to provide liquidity, primarily related to loan growth.&nbsp;&nbsp;Average s</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:11pt;">ubordinated debt</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:11pt;"> pricing increased 175</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:11pt;"> basis points</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:11pt;">, and the average balance increased from $7.2 million at December 31, 2013 to $12.9 million at December 31, 2014.&nbsp;&nbsp;This net increase was primarily due to a new $6.5 million, 5.5%, amortizing note issued to retire preferred stock during the first quarter of 2014 and offset by the payoff of a $2 million, 1.6% note during the third quarter of 2014.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 11pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:11pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 11pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:11pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 11pt">

		</p>

			<font style="display: inline;font-size:11pt;">The provision for loan losses is based upon management&#x2019;s estimate of the amount required to maintain an adequate allowance for loan losses as discussed within the Critical Accounting Policies section above.&nbsp;&nbsp;The provision for loan losses for the year ended December 31, 2014, resulted in a recovery of $352 thousand compared to a recovery of $186 thousand for the year ended December 31, 2013, reflecting improvements realized in loan quality.&nbsp;&nbsp;Changes in the amount of provision for loan losses during each period reflect the results of the Bank&#x2019;s analysis used to determine the adequacy of the allowance for loan losses.&nbsp;&nbsp;We are committed to making loan loss provisions that maintain an allowance which adequately reflects the risk inherent in our loan portfolio.&nbsp;&nbsp;This commitment is more fully discussed in the &#x201C;Asset Quality&#x201D; section below.</font>

		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 11pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:11pt;">Noninterest income decreased $580 thousand to $1.8 million for the year ended December 31, 2014 compared to $2.4 million for the same period in 2013.&nbsp;&nbsp;The primary cause of the decrease in noninterest income related to our wholesale mortgage operation, which provided gains on sales of loans of $55 thousand in 2014 compared to $798 thousand in 2013.&nbsp;&nbsp;During the first quarter of 2014, the Company closed its wholesale mortgage operation because the slowdown in the mortgage originations business coupled with the increased regulatory burden made the business difficult to sustain.&nbsp; </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 11pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:11pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 11pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;font-size:11pt;">Noninterest Expense</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 11pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:11pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 11pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;font-size:11pt;">Year ended December 31, 2014 compared to year ended December 31, 2013</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 11pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:11pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 11pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:11pt;">Noninterest expense includes all expenses other than interest paid on deposits and borrowings.&nbsp;&nbsp;Total noninterest expense remained relatively consistent overall, and increased just 0.96% or $143 thousand to $15.1 million for 2014 compared to $14.9 million for 2013.&nbsp;&nbsp;Noninterest expense was 2.61% of average assets for the year ended December 31, 2014 compared to 2.79% for the year ended December 31, 2013.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 11pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:11pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 11pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:11pt;">The mix of noninterest expense changed with a decrease in salaries and employee benefits of 3.71% to $8.6 million for 2014 compared to $9.0 million for 2013, due primarily to decreased stock-based compensation.&nbsp;&nbsp;This decrease was offset by a net 8% increase in other noninterest expenses which reflects the overall growth in operations, including the opening of a new branch in June 2014.</font>
		</p>

			<font style="display: inline;font-size:11pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 11pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;font-size:11pt;">Income Taxes</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 11pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:11pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 11pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:11pt;">Our reported income tax expense was $2.1 million for 2014 compared to $1.8 million for 2013.&nbsp;&nbsp;Note 11 of our consolidated financial statements included elsewhere in this Report on Form 10-K provides a reconciliation between the amount of income tax benefit/expense computed using the federal statutory rate and our actual income tax benefit/expense.&nbsp;&nbsp;Also included in Note 11 to the consolidated financial statements is information regarding the principal items giving rise to deferred taxes for the two years ended December 31, 2014 and 2013.</font>
		</p>

			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-size:11pt;">Financial Condition</font>

			<font style="display: inline;font-size:11pt;">&nbsp;</font>

		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 11pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;font-size:11pt;">Assets</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 11pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:11pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 11pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:11pt;">Total assets increased to $598.5 million at December 31, 2014, compared to $547.9 million at December 31, 2013, representing an increase of $50.7 million or 9.25%, related primarily to loan growth.&nbsp;&nbsp;Average assets increased 7.80%, related primarily to growth in average loans outstanding, from $534.3 million for the year ended December 31, 2013 to $576.0 million for the year ended December 31, 2014.&nbsp;&nbsp;Stockholders&#x2019; equity was $49.7 million at December 31, 2013 and decreased $30 thousand during 2014.&nbsp;&nbsp;The decrease in stockholders&#x2019; equity despite net income of $4.4 million was due primarily to the redemption of the Company&#x2019;s outstanding preferred stock during 2014.&nbsp; </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 11pt">

</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:11pt;">Commercial real estate loans increased $</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:11pt;">17.5</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:11pt;"> million or </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:11pt;">10.59</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:11pt;">% to $</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:11pt;">182.7</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:11pt;"> million and represented 3</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:11pt;">7.92</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:11pt;">% of the portfolio.&nbsp; </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:11pt;">Commercial loans increased $1</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:11pt;">0.9 million, or 19.52%, to $66.9</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:11pt;"> million and represented 13.88% of the loan portfolio.&nbsp; </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:11pt;">Other construction, land dev</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:11pt;">elopment and other land loans in</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:11pt;">creased $</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:11pt;">9.7</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:11pt;"> million, or </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:11pt;">22.38</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:11pt;">%, to $</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:11pt;">52.9</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:11pt;"> million from $</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:11pt;">43.3</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:11pt;"> million and represented </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:11pt;">10.99</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:11pt;">% of the portfolio.&nbsp;&nbsp;The allowance for loan losses was $</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:11pt;">7.9</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:11pt;"> million, </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:11pt;">down</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:11pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:11pt;">3.56</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:11pt;">% from the prior year and represented 1</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:11pt;">.63</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:11pt;">% of total loans outstanding at December 31, 201</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:11pt;">4,</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:11pt;"> down from </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:11pt;">1.89</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:11pt;">% at December 31, 201</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:11pt;">3, reflecting improvements in loan quality</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:11pt;">.</font>

Other real estate owned declined $848 thousand or 31.90% from $2.7 million at December 31, 2013 to $1.8 million at December 31, 2014.</font>
		</p>

			<font style="display: inline;font-size:11pt;">Resources continue to be devoted specifically to the ongoing review of the loan portfolio and the workouts of problem assets to minimize any losses to the Company. The Company has in place a special assets loan committee, which includes the Co</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:11pt;">mpany&#x2019;s Chief Executive Officer and</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:11pt;"> Chief Credit Officer. This committee </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:11pt;">approves</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:11pt;"> strategies and all credit actions taken on significant problem loans. Management continues to monitor delinquencies, risk rating changes, charge-offs, market trends and other indicators of risk in the Company&#x2019;s portfolio, particularly those tied to residential and commercial real estate, and adjusts the allowance for loan losses accordingly. The Company work</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:11pt;">s</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:11pt;"> with its customers on loan collection matters while taking appropriate actions to improve the Company&#x2019;s position and minimize any losses. These </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:11pt;">problem </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:11pt;">loans are closely managed and evaluated for collection with appropriate loss reserves established whenever necessary. </font>

		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;;font-size: 11pt"><font style="display: inline;font-size:11pt;"></font><font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;font-size:11pt;">Non-performing Assets</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 11pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:11pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 11pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:11pt;">At December 31, 2014, non-performing assets decreased $1.9 million or 26.46% to $5.2 million at December 31, 2014 compared to $7.1 million at December 31, 2013.&nbsp;&nbsp;The ratio of nonperforming assets to total assets was 0.88% at year end 2014 compared to 1.30% at year end 2013.&nbsp;&nbsp;Non-performing assets consist of nonaccrual loans totaling $3.4 million and OREO of $1.8 million which consists of approximately 53 residential building lots.&nbsp; </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 11pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:11pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 11pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:11pt;">We place loans on non-accrual when the collection of principal and interest is doubtful, generally when a loan becomes 90 days past due.&nbsp;&nbsp;There are three negative implications for earnings when we place a loan on non-accrual status.&nbsp;&nbsp;First, all interest accrued but unpaid at the date that the loan is placed on non-accrual status is either deducted from interest income or written off as a loss.&nbsp;&nbsp;Second, accruals on interest are discontinued until it becomes certain that both principal and interest can be repaid.&nbsp;&nbsp;Finally, there may be actual losses that require additional provisions for loan losses to be charged against earnings.</font>
		</p>

		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 11pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:11pt;">The allowance for loan losses at December 31, 2014 was $7.9 million compared to $8.2 million at December 31, 2013.&nbsp;&nbsp;The allowance for loan losses was 1.63% of total loans outstanding at December 31, 2014 compared to 1.89% at December 31, 2013.&nbsp;&nbsp;The recovery of provision for loan losses was $352 thousand for 2014 compared to $186 thousand for 2013.&nbsp;&nbsp;Net charge-offs resulted in a net recovery of $61 thousand for the year ended December 31, 2014 and net recoveries of $1.1 million for the year ended December 31, 2013.&nbsp;&nbsp;Management feels that the stress of the portfolio has decreased reflecting the recovery of the real estate market in the Richmond metropolitan area and management&#x2019;s focus on improving asset quality.&nbsp;&nbsp;Additional provision for loan losses may be required if a downward trend in conditions returns.&nbsp;&nbsp;We have no exposure to sub-prime loans in the portfolio.&nbsp; </font>
		</p>

			<font style="display: inline;font-size:11pt;">We have various lines of credit available from certain of our correspondent banks in the aggregate amount of $35.0 million.&nbsp;&nbsp;These lines of credit, which bear interest at prevailing market rates, permit us to borrow funds in the overnight market, and are renewable annually.&nbsp; </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 11pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:11pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 11pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;font-size:11pt;">Interest Rate Sensitivity</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 11pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:11pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 11pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:11pt;">The most important element of asset/liability management is the monitoring of the Company&#x2019;s sensitivity to interest rate movements.&nbsp;&nbsp;The income stream of the Company is subject to risk resulting from interest rate fluctuations to the extent there is a difference between the amount of the Company&#x2019;s interest earning assets and the amount of interest bearing liabilities that are prepaid, mature or repriced in specific periods.&nbsp;&nbsp;Our goal is to maximize net interest income within acceptable levels of risk to changes in interest rates.&nbsp;&nbsp;We seek to meet this goal by influencing the maturity and re-pricing characteristics of the various lending and deposit taking lines of business and by managing discretionary balance sheet asset and liability portfolios.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 11pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:11pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 11pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:11pt;">We monitor interest rate levels on a daily basis at meetings of the Asset Liability Committee.&nbsp;&nbsp;The following reports and/or tools are used to assess the current interest rate environment and its impact on our earnings and liquidity:&nbsp;&nbsp;monthly and year to date net interest margin and spread calculations, monthly and year to date balance sheet and income statements versus budget, quarterly net portfolio value analysis, a weekly survey of rates offered by other local competitive institutions and gap analysis (matching maturities or repricing dates of interest sensitive assets to those of interest sensitive liabilities by periods) and a Risk Manager model used to measure earnings at risk and economic value of equity at risk.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 11pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:11pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 11pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:11pt;">The data in the following table reflects repricing or expected maturities of various assets and liabilities.&nbsp;&nbsp;The gap analysis represents the difference between interest-sensitive assets and liabilities in a specific time interval.&nbsp;&nbsp;Interest sensitivity gap analysis presents a position that existed at one particular point in time, and assumes that assets and liabilities with similar repricing characteristics will reprice at the same time and to the same degree.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 1pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:1pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>

		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 11pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;font-size:11pt;">Capital Resources and Dividends</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 11pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:11pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 11pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:11pt;">We have an ongoing strategic objective of maintaining a capital base that supports the pursuit of profitable business opportunities, provides resources to absorb risk inherent in our activities and meets or exceeds all regulatory requirements.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 11pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:11pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 11pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:11pt;">The Federal Reserve Board has established minimum regulatory capital standards for bank holding companies and state member banks.&nbsp;&nbsp;The regulatory capital standards categorize assets and off-balance sheet items into four categories that weight balance sheet assets according to risk, requiring more capital for holding higher risk assets.&nbsp;&nbsp;At December 31, 2014 and 2013, the Company&#x2019;s Tier 1 leverage ratio (Tier 1 capital to average total assets) was 9.22% and 10.04%, respectively, with the minimum regulatory ratio to be well capitalized at 5.00%.&nbsp;&nbsp;Tier 1 risk based capital ratios at December 31, 2014 and 2013 were 11.00% and 12.34%, respectively, with the minimum regulatory ratio to be well capitalized at 6.00%.&nbsp;&nbsp;Total risk based capital to risk weighted assets at December 31, 2014 and 2013 were 13.54% and 13.78%, respectively, with the minimum regulatory ratio to be well capitalized at 10.00%.&nbsp;&nbsp;Our capital structure exceeds regulatory guidelines established for well capitalized institutions, which affords us the opportunity to take advantage of business opportunities while ensuring that we have the resources to protect against risk inherent in our business.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 11pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:11pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 11pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:11pt;">The Company&#x2019;s primary focus during 2014 was balance sheet management through controlled, quality loan growth and capital preservation.&nbsp;&nbsp;Despite 22.62%</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:11pt;"> growth in the loan portfolio, the Company was able to </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:11pt;">maintain </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:11pt;">total risk based capital by employing a strategy focused on detailed management of all aspects of the balance sheet.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>

		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 11pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;font-size:11pt;">Liquidity</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 11pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:11pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 11pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:11pt;">Liquidity represents an institution&#x2019;s ability to meet present and future financial obligations through either the sale or maturity of existing assets or the acquisition of additional funds through liability management.&nbsp;&nbsp;Liquid assets include cash, interest-bearing deposits with banks, federal funds sold, short-term investments, securities classified as available for sale as well as loans and securities maturing within one year.&nbsp;&nbsp;As a result of our management of liquid assets and the ability to generate liquidity through liability funding, management believes we maintain overall liquidity sufficient to satisfy our depositors&#x2019; requirements and meet our clients&#x2019; credit needs.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 11pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:11pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 11pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:11pt;">We also maintain additional sources of liquidity through a variety of borrowing arrangements.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Bank maintains federal funds lines with a large regional money-center banking institution and a local community bankers bank.&nbsp;&nbsp;These available lines currently total $35.0 million, of which there were $6.3 million outstanding draws at December 31, 2014. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 11pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:11pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 11pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:11pt;">We have a credit line with the FHLB in the amount of approximately $76.5 million, without pledging additional collateral, which may be used for short and/or long-term borrowing.&nbsp;&nbsp;Advances from the FHLB totaled $45.0 million at December 31, 2014.&nbsp; </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 11pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:11pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 11pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:11pt;">At December 31, 2014, cash and cash equivalents, available federal funds, collateral-free securities, and available FHLB advances were 30.31% of total deposits, down from 32.68% at December 31, 2013.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 11pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:11pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 11pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:11pt;">Maintaining liquidity at levels to cover any eventuality has been a primary goal, and we feel that the levels maintained during 2014 and 2013 accomplish that goal.</font>
		</p>

Based on that evaluation, the Chief Executive Officer and Chief Financial Officer have concluded that the Company&#x2019;s disclosure controls and procedures were effective as of December&nbsp;31, 2014 to ensure that information required to be disclosed by the Company in reports that it files or submits under the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 is recorded, processed, summarized and reported within the time periods specified in Securities and Exchange Commission rules and forms. </font>

Integrated Framework issued by the Committee of Sponsoring Organizations of the Treadway Commission</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:11pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:11pt;">(1992) </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:11pt;">(&#x201C;COSO&#x201D;). </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:11pt;"> Further, t</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:11pt;">here were no changes in the Company&#x2019;s internal control over financial reporting during the Company&#x2019;s </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:11pt;">year</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:11pt;"> ended December&nbsp;31, 2014 that have materially affected, or are reasonably likely to materially affect, the Company&#x2019;s internal control over financial reporting.&nbsp;&nbsp;Based on our assessment</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:11pt;"> described herein</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:11pt;">, we believe that, as of December 31, 2014, the Company&#x2019;s internal control over financial reporting was effective based on </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:11pt;">the foregoing</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:11pt;"> criteria.</font>

		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">We have audited the accompanying consolidated statements of financial condition of First Capital Bancorp, Inc. and Subsidiary (the &#x201C;C</font><font style="display: inline;">ompany&#x201D;) as of December 31, 2014 and 2013</font><font style="display: inline;">, and the related consolidated statements of operations, comprehensive income, stockholders&#x2019; equity, and cash flows for each of the years in the two-year period ended December 31, 201</font><font style="display: inline;">4</font><font style="display: inline;">.&nbsp; These consolidated financial statements are the responsibility of the Company&#x2019;s management. Our responsibility is to express an opinion on these consolidated financial statements based on our audits.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">

		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">We conducted our audits in accordance with the standards of the Public Company Accounting Oversight Board (United States). Those standards require that we plan and perform our audits to obtain reasonable assurance about whether the consolidated financial statements are free of material misstatement.&nbsp; The Company is not required to have, nor were we engaged to perform, an audit of its internal control over financial reporting.&nbsp; Our audits included consideration of internal control over financial reporting as a basis for designing audit procedures that are appropriate in the circumstances, but not for the purpose of expressing an opinion on the effectiveness of the Company&#x2019;s internal control over financial reporting. Accordingly, we express no such opinion.&nbsp; An audit includes examining, on a test basis, evidence supporting the amounts and disclosures in the consolidated financial statements. An audit also includes assessing the accounting principles used and significant estimates made by management, as well as evaluating the overall consolidated financial statement presentation.&nbsp; We believe that our audits provide a reasonable basis for our opinion. </font>
		</p>

		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">In our opinion, the consolidated financial statements referred to above present fairly, in all material respects, the financial position of First Capital Bancorp, Inc. and Su</font><font style="display: inline;">bsidiary as of December 31, 2014 and 2013</font><font style="display: inline;"> and the results of their operations and their cash flows for each of the years in the two-yea</font><font style="display: inline;">r period ended December 31, 2014</font><font style="display: inline;">, in conformity with accounting principles generally accepted in the United States of America.</font>

		<p style="margin:0pt;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;color:#00B050;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 1pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>

		<p style="margin:0pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;color:#00B050;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 1pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>

		<p style="margin:0pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;color:#000000;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;color:#000000;font-size:12pt;">Note 1 &#x2013; </font><a name="NotesToFinancialStatements"></a><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;color:#000000;font-size:12pt;">Summary of Significant Accounting Policies</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;color:#000000;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Fi</font><font style="display: inline;">rst Capital Bancorp, Inc. (the Company</font><font style="display: inline;">) is the holding company of and succes</font><font style="display: inline;">sor to First Capital Bank (the Bank</font><font style="display: inline;">).&nbsp; </font><font style="display: inline;">In 2006, the C</font><font style="display: inline;">ompany acquired all of the outstanding stock of the Bank in a statutory s</font><font style="display: inline;">hare exchange transaction </font><font style="display: inline;">pursuant to an Agreement and Plan of Reorganization, between</font><font style="display: inline;"> the Company and the Bank (the Agreement</font><font style="display: inline;">).&nbsp;&nbsp;Under the terms of the Agreement, the shares of the Bank&#x2019;s common stock were exchanged for shares of the Company</font><font style="display: inline;">&#x2019;s common stock</font><font style="display: inline;"> on a </font><font style="display: inline;">one</font><font style="display: inline;">-for-one basis.&nbsp;&nbsp;As a result, the Bank became a wholly owned subsidiary of the Company, the Company became the holding company of the Bank</font><font style="display: inline;">,</font><font style="display: inline;"> and the shareholders of the Bank became shareholders of the Company.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:12pt;">The Company conducts all of its business activities through the branch offices of its wholly owned subsidiary, First Capital Bank.&nbsp;&nbsp;First Capital Bank created RE1, LLC, and RE2, LLC, wholly owned Virginia limited liability companies for the sole purpose of taking title to property acquired in lieu of foreclosure.&nbsp;&nbsp;RE1, LLC and RE2, LLC have been consolidated with First Capital Bank.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company exists primarily for the purpose of holding the stock of its subsidiary, the Bank, and such other subsidiaries as it may acquire or establish</font><font style="display: inline;">. &nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 11pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:12pt;">The Company has one other wholly owned subsidiar</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:12pt;">y, FCRV Statutory Trust 1 (the Trust</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:12pt;">), a Delaware Business Trust that was formed in connection with the issuance of trust preferred debt in 2006.&nbsp;&nbsp;Pursuant to current accounting standards, the Company does not consolidate the Trust.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:12pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:12pt;">The accounting and reporting policies of the Company and its wholly owned subsidiary conform to accounting principles generally accepted in the United States of America and general practices within the financial services industry.&nbsp;&nbsp;The following is a summary of the more significant of these policies</font><font style="display: inline;">.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">Consolidation</font><font style="display: inline;"> &#x2013; The consolidated financial statements include the accounts of First Capital Bancorp, Inc. and its wholly owned subsidiary.&nbsp;&nbsp;All material intercompany balances and transactions have been eliminated.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">Use of estimates</font><font style="display: inline;"> &nbsp;&#x2013;</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">To prepare financial statements in conformity with accounting principles generally accepted in the United States of America management makes estimates and assumptions based on available information.&nbsp;&nbsp;These estimates and assumptions affect the amounts reported in the consolidated financial statements and the disclosures provided, and actual results could differ.&nbsp;&nbsp;The allowance for loan losses, valuation of other real estate owned (OREO), and fair values of financial instruments are particularly subject to change.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">Cash equivalents</font><font style="display: inline;"> &#x2013; </font><font style="display: inline;">Cash and cash equivalents include cash, deposits with other financial institutions, and federal funds sold</font><font style="display: inline;"> with original maturities of three months or less</font><font style="display: inline;">.&nbsp;&nbsp;Net cash flows are reported for loans, deposits, federal funds purchased, Federal Home Loan Bank (FHLB) borrowings, and repurchase agreements.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:normal;font-size:12pt;">Investment Securities</font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;font-size:12pt;"> &#x2013; Investment in debt securities classified as held-to-maturity are stated at cost, adjusted for amortization or premiums and accretion of discounts using the interest method.&nbsp;&nbsp;Management has a positive intent and ability to hold these securities to maturity and, accordingly, adjustments are not made for temporary declines in their fair value below amortized cost.&nbsp;&nbsp;Investments not classified as held-to-maturity are classified as available-for-sale.&nbsp;&nbsp;Debt securities classified as available-for-sale are stated at fair value with unrealized holding gains and losses excluded from earnings and reported, net of deferred tax, as a component of other comprehensive income until realized.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">

		</p>
		<p><font size="1"> </font></p><div style="width:100%">

		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:center;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 11pt">

			<font style="display: inline;">F-</font><font style="display: inline;">10</font>

		</p>

		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 11pt">

			&nbsp;

		</p>

</div><hr size="3" style="color:#999999" width="100%" align="center"></hr><p style="page-break-after:always">&nbsp;</p><div style="width:100%">

		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 11pt">

			&nbsp;

		</p>

</div>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;;font-size: 12pt"><font style="display: inline;"></font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Interest income includes amortization of purchase premium or discount.&nbsp;&nbsp;Premiums and discounts on securities are amortized on the level-yield method without anticipating prepayments, except for mortgage-backed securities where prepayments are anticipated.&nbsp;&nbsp;Gains and losses on sales are recorded on the trade date and determined using the specific identification method.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Management evaluates securities for other-than-temporary impairment (OTTI) on at least a quarterly basis, and more frequently when economic or market conditions warrant such an evaluation.&nbsp; For securities in an unrealized loss position, management considers the extent and duration of the unrealized loss, and the financial condition and near-term prospects of the issuer.&nbsp;&nbsp;Management also assesses whether it intends to sell, or it is more likely than not that it will be required to sell, a security in an unrealized loss position before recovery of its amortized cost basis. If either of the criteria regarding intent or requirement to sell is met, the entire difference between amortized cost and fair value is recognized as impairment through earnings.&nbsp; For debt securities that do not meet the aforementioned criteria, the amount of impairment is split into two components as follows: 1) OTTI related to credit loss, which must be recognized in the income statement and 2) OTTI related to other factors, which is recognized in other comprehensive income.&nbsp; The credit loss is defined as the difference between the present value of the cash flows expected to be collected and the amortized cost basis. For equity securities, the entire amount of impairment is recognized through earnings.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Due to the nature of, and restrictions placed upon the Company&#x2019;s common stock investment in the Federal Reserve Bank, FHLB and Community Bankers Bank, these securities have been classified as restricted equity securities and carried at cost.&nbsp;&nbsp;These restricted securities are not subject to the investment security classifications, but are periodically evaluated for impairment based on ultimate recovery of par value.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Management uses available information to recognize losses on loans; future additions to the allowances may be necessary based on changes in local economic conditions.&nbsp;&nbsp;In addition, regulatory agencies, as an integral part of their examination process, periodically review the Bank&#x2019;s allowance for losses on loans. Such agencies may require the Bank to recognize additions to the allowances based on their judgments about information available to them at the time of their examination. Because of these factors, it is reasonably possible that the allowance for losses on loans may change in the near term.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 11pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">Loans and allowances for loan losses</font><font style="display: inline;"> - Loans are concentrated to borrowers in the Richmond metropolitan area and are stated at the amount of unpaid principal reduced by an allowance for loan losses.&nbsp;&nbsp;Interest on loans is calculated by using the simple interest method on daily balances on the principal amount outstanding. The accrual of interest on loans is discontinued when, in the opinion of management, there is an indication that the borrower may be unable to meet payments as they become due.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company defers loan origination and commitment fees, net of certain direct loan origination costs, and the net deferred fees are amortized into interest income over the lives of the related loans as yield adjustments.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Loans that are 90 days or more past due are individually reviewed for ultimate collectibility.&nbsp;&nbsp;Interest determined to be uncollectible on loans that are contractually past due is charged off, or an allowance is established based on management&#x2019;s periodic evaluation.&nbsp;&nbsp;The allowance is established by a charge to interest income equal to all interest previously accrued, and income is subsequently recognized only to the extent that cash payments are received until, in management&#x2019;s judgment, the borrower&#x2019;s ability to make periodic interest and principal payments is returned to normal, in which case the loan is returned to accrual status.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">

		</p>
		<p><font size="1"> </font></p><div style="width:100%">

		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:center;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 11pt">

			<font style="display: inline;">F-</font><font style="display: inline;">11</font>

		</p>

		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 11pt">

			&nbsp;

		</p>

</div><hr size="3" style="color:#999999" width="100%" align="center"></hr><p style="page-break-after:always">&nbsp;</p><div style="width:100%">

		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 11pt">

			&nbsp;

		</p>

</div>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;;font-size: 12pt"><font style="display: inline;"></font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">A loan is defined as impaired when, based on current information and events, it is probable that the creditor will be unable to collect all amounts of principal and interest when due according to the contractual terms of the loan agreement.&nbsp;&nbsp;Impairment is measured either by discounting the expected future cash flows at the loan&#x2019;s effective interest rate, based on the net realizable value of the collateral or based upon an observable market price where applicable.&nbsp;&nbsp;Charges on impaired loans are recognized as a component of the allowance for loans losses.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The allowance for loan losses is maintained at a level considered by management to be adequate to absorb known and expected loan losses currently inherent in the loan portfolio.&nbsp;&nbsp;Management's assessment of the adequacy of the allowance is based upon type and volume of the loan portfolio, existing and anticipated economic conditions, and other factors which deserve current recognition in estimating loan losses.&nbsp;&nbsp;The allowance is increased by a provision for loan losses, which is charged to expense, and reduced by charge-offs, net of recoveries.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">Loans Held for Sale </font><font style="display: inline;">&#x2014; Loans </font><font style="display: inline;">originated and intended for sale in the secondary market are carried at the lower of aggregate cost or fair value, as determined by aggregate outstanding commitments from investors or current investor yield requirements.&nbsp;&nbsp;Net unrealized losses are recognized through a valuation allowance by charges to income.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Gains or losses on sales of mortgage loans are recognized based on the difference between the selling price and the carrying value of the related mortgage loans sold.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company typically releases the mortgage servicing rights when the loans are sold.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The Company accounts for the transfer of financial assets in accordance with authoritative accounting guidance which is based on consistent application of a financial-components approach that recognizes the financial and servicing assets the Company controls and the liabilities the Company has incurred, derecognizes financial assets when control has been surrendered and derecognizes liabilities when extinguished.&nbsp;&nbsp;The guidance provides consistent guidelines for distinguishing transfers of financial assets from transfers that are secured borrowings.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">As is customary in such sales, the Company provides indemnifications to the buyers under certain circumstances. These indemnifications may include repurchase of loans.&nbsp;&nbsp;No repurchases and losses during the last two years have been experienced; accordingly, no provision is made for losses at the time of sale.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The Company enters into commitments to originate loans whereby the interest rate on the loan is determined prior to funding (rate lock commitments).&nbsp;&nbsp;Rate lock commitments on mortgage loans that are intended to be sold are considered to be derivatives.&nbsp;&nbsp;Time elapsing between issuance of a loan commitment and closing and sale of the loan generally ranges from </font><font style="display: inline;">5</font><font style="display: inline;"> to </font><font style="display: inline;">20</font><font style="display: inline;"> days.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company protects itself from changes in interest rates through the use of best efforts forward delivery contracts, whereby the Company commits to sell a loan at the time the borrower commits to an interest rate with the intent that the buyer has assumed interest rate risk on the loan.&nbsp;&nbsp;As a result, the Company is not exposed to losses nor will we realize significant gains related to the rate lock commitments due to changes in interest rates.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">

		</p>
		<p><font size="1"> </font></p><div style="width:100%">

		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:center;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 11pt">

			<font style="display: inline;">F-</font><font style="display: inline;">12</font>

		</p>

		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 11pt">

			&nbsp;

		</p>

</div><hr size="3" style="color:#999999" width="100%" align="center"></hr><p style="page-break-after:always">&nbsp;</p><div style="width:100%">

		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 11pt">

			&nbsp;

		</p>

</div>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;;font-size: 12pt"><font style="display: inline;"></font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The market value of rate lock commitments and best efforts contracts is not readily ascertainable with precision because rate lock commitments and best efforts contracts are not actively traded in stand-alone markets.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company determines the fair value of rate lock commitments and best efforts contracts by measuring the change in the value of the underlying asset while taking into consideration the probability that the rate lock commitments will close.&nbsp;&nbsp;Due to high correlation between rate lock commitments and best efforts contracts, no significant gains or losses have occurred on the rate lock commitments for the years ended December 31, 2014, and 2013.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">Other real estate owned</font><font style="display: inline;"> &nbsp;&#x2013;</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">OREO is comprised of real estate properties acquired in partial or total satisfaction of problem loans.&nbsp;&nbsp;The properties are recorded at fair value less cost to sell at the date of foreclosure, establishing a new cost basis for the asset.&nbsp;&nbsp;Losses arising at the time of acquisition of such properties are charged against the allowance for loan losses.&nbsp;&nbsp;Subsequent to foreclosure, valuations are periodically performed by management and the properties are carried at the lower of carrying amount or fair value less cost to sell.&nbsp;&nbsp;Subsequent write-downs that may be required to the carrying value of these properties are charged to current operations.&nbsp;&nbsp;Gains and losses realized from the sale of OREO are included in current operations.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">Bank premises and equipment</font><font style="display: inline;"> &nbsp;-</font><font style="display: inline;"> Company premises and equipment are stated at cost, less accumulated depreciation. Depreciation of Company premises and equipment is computed on the straight-line method over estimated useful lives of </font><font style="display: inline;">10</font><font style="display: inline;"> to </font><font style="display: inline;">39</font><font style="display: inline;"> years for premises and </font><font style="display: inline;">3</font><font style="display: inline;"> to </font><font style="display: inline;">10</font><font style="display: inline;"> years for equipment, furniture and fixtures. Main</font><font style="display: inline;">tenance and repairs are charged to expense as incurred and major improvements are capital</font><font style="display: inline;">ized.&nbsp;&nbsp;Upon sale or retirement of depreci</font><font style="display: inline;">able properties, the cost and related accumulated depreciation are netted against the proceeds and any result</font><font style="display: inline;">ing gain or loss is included in the determination of income.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">Impairment or Disposal of Long-Lived Assets - </font><font style="display: inline;">The Company&#x2019;s long-lived assets are reviewed for impairment whenever events or changes in circumstances indicate that the carrying amount of an asset may not be recoverable.&nbsp;&nbsp;Recoverability of assets to be held and used, such as bank premises and equipment, is measured by a comparison of the carrying amount of an asset to future net cash flows expected to be generated by the asset.&nbsp;&nbsp;If the carrying amount of an asset exceeds its estimated future cash flows, an impairment charge is recognized in the amount by which the carrying amount of the asset exceed the fair value of the asset.&nbsp;&nbsp;Assets to be disposed of, such as foreclosed properties, are reported at the lower of the carrying amount or fair value less costs to sell.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">Bank-owned life insurance</font><font style="display: inline;"> &#x2013; The Bank owns life insurance </font><font style="display: inline;">policies on key employees with a</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">total </font><font style="display: inline;">face amount of $</font><font style="display: inline;">22.7</font><font style="display: inline;"> million</font><font style="display: inline;">.&nbsp;&nbsp;The bank owned life insurance (BOLI) policies are recorded at their cash surrender values of </font><font style="display: inline;">$9.9</font><font style="display: inline;"> million and $9.6 million at December 31, 2014 and 2013, respectively.&nbsp;&nbsp;Income generated from these policies is recorded as noninterest income.&nbsp; </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">Stock-Based Compensation &#x2013; </font><font style="display: inline;">Compensation cost is recognized for stock options and restricted stock awards issued to employees, based on the fair value of these awards at the date of grant. The Black-Scholes model is used to estimate the fair value of stock options, while the market price of the Company&#x2019;s common stock at the date of grant is used for restricted stock awards. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:9pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Compensation cost is recognized over the required service period, generally defined as the vesting period. For awards with graded vesting, compensation cost is recognized on a straight-line basis over the requisite service period for the entire award.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">

		</p>
		<p><font size="1"> </font></p><div style="width:100%">

		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:center;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 11pt">

			<font style="display: inline;">F-</font><font style="display: inline;">13</font>

		</p>

			&nbsp;

		</p>

</div>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;;font-size: 12pt"><font style="display: inline;"></font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">Income taxes -</font><font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">Income tax expense is the total of the current year income tax due or refundable, and the change in deferred tax assets and liabilities.&nbsp;&nbsp;Deferred tax assets and liabilities are the expected future tax amounts for the temporary differences between carrying amounts and tax bases of assets and liabilities, computed using enacted tax rates.&nbsp;&nbsp;A valuation allowance, if needed, reduces deferred tax assets to the amount expected to be realized.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:9pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">A tax position is recognized as a benefit only if it is &#x201C;more likely than not&#x201D; that the tax position would be sustained in a tax examination, with a tax examination being presumed to occur.&nbsp;&nbsp;The amount recognized is the largest amount of tax benefit that is greater than </font><font style="display: inline;">50</font><font style="display: inline;">% likely of being realized on examination.&nbsp;&nbsp;For tax positions not meeting the &#x201C;more likely than not&#x201D; test, no tax benefit is recorded.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:9pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;font-size:12pt;">The Company recognizes interest and/or penalties related to income tax matters in income tax expense.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">Advertising costs -</font><font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">Advertising costs are expensed in the period they are incurred and amounted to </font><font style="display: inline;">$487</font><font style="display: inline;"> thousand and </font><font style="display: inline;">$397</font><font style="display: inline;"> thousand for the years ended December 31, 2014 and 2013, respectively.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">Earnings Per Common Share</font><font style="display: inline;">&#x2014;Earnings per common share represents net income allocable to stockholders, which represents net income less dividends paid or payable to preferred stock shareholders, divided by the weighted-average number of common shares outstanding during the period.&nbsp;&nbsp;For diluted earnings per common share, net income allocable to common shareholders is divided by the weighted average number of common </font><font style="display: inline;">shares </font><font style="display: inline;">issued and outstanding for each period plus amounts representing the dilutive effect of stock options and restricted stock, as well as any adjustment to income that would result from the assumed issuance.&nbsp;&nbsp;The effects of restricted stock and stock options are excluded from the computation of diluted earnings per common share in periods in which the effect would be antidilutive.&nbsp;&nbsp;Potential common shares that may be issued relate solely to outstanding stock options, warrants, and restricted stock and are determined using the treasury stock method.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">Comprehensive Income</font><font style="display: inline;"> &#x2013; Comprehensive income consists of net income and other comprehensive income.&nbsp;&nbsp;Other comprehensive income includes unrealized gains and losses on securities available for sale which are also recognized as separate components of equity.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:9pt;text-decoration:underline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">Loss Contingencies &#x2013; </font><font style="display: inline;">Loss contingencies, including claims and legal actions arising in the ordinary course of business, are recorded as liabilities when the likelihood of loss is probable and an amount or range of loss can be reasonably estimated.&nbsp;&nbsp;Management believes there are no such matters that will have a material effect on the consolidated financial statements.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 11pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:11pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">Fair Value of Financial Instruments </font><font style="display: inline;">&#x2013; Fair values of financial instruments are estimated using relevant market information and other assumptions, as more fully disclosed in a separate note.&nbsp;&nbsp;Fair value estimates involve uncertainties and matters of significant judgment regarding interest rates, credit risk, prepayments, and other factors, especially in the absence of broad markets for particular items.&nbsp;&nbsp;Changes in assumptions or in market conditions could significantly affect these estimates.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">Recently Issued Accounting Pronouncements</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">On July&nbsp;18, 2013, the FASB issued ASU No.&nbsp;2013-11, </font><font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">Income Taxes (Topic 740): Presentation of an unrecognized tax benefit when a net operating loss carryforward or tax credit carryforward exists</font><font style="display: inline;">. ASU 2013-11 will be effective for reporting periods beginning after December&nbsp;15, 2013 and clarifies Topic 740.&nbsp;This ASU requires companies to present an unrecognized tax benefit, or portion thereof, for a net operating loss or tax credit carryforward as a reduction of a deferred tax asset. The adoption of this ASU had no impact on the Company&#x2019;s consolidated financial statements.</font>
		</p>
