		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">In January 2014, the FASB issued Accounting Standards Update (ASU) No. 2014-04, </font><font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">Receivables &#x2013; Troubled Debt Restructurings by Creditors (subtopic 310-40) &#x2013; Reclassification of Residential Real Estate Collateralized Consumer Mortgage Loans upon Foreclosure.&nbsp; </font><font style="display: inline;">The amendments are intended to clarify when a creditor should be considered to have received physical possession of residential real estate property collateralizing a consumer mortgage loan such that the loan should be derecognized and the real estate recognized.&nbsp;&nbsp;These amendments clarify that an in substance repossession for foreclosure occurs, and a creditor is considered to have received physical possession of residential real estate property collateralizing a consumer mortgage loan, upon either:&nbsp;&nbsp;(a) the creditor obtaining legal title to the residential real estate property upon completion of a foreclosure; or (b) the borrower conveying all interest in the residential real estate property to the creditor to satisfy that loan through completion of a deed in lieu of foreclosure or through a similar legal agreement.&nbsp;&nbsp;Additional disclosures are required.&nbsp;&nbsp;The amendments are effective for public business entities for annual periods and interim periods within those annual periods beginning after December 15, 2014.&nbsp;&nbsp;The adoption of this ASU is not expected to have a material impact on the Company&#x2019;s consolidated financial statements.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">In May 2014, the FASB issued ASU No. 2014-09, </font><font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">Revenue from Contracts with Customers (Topic 606).&nbsp; </font><font style="display: inline;">The guidance in this update supersedes the revenue recognition requirements in Topic 605, </font><font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">Revenue Recognition</font><font style="display: inline;">, and most industry-specific guidance throughout the Industry Topics of Codification.&nbsp;&nbsp;The guidance in this update affects any entity that either enters into contracts with customers to transfer goods or services or enters into contracts for the transfer of non-financial assets.&nbsp;&nbsp;This amendment is intended to clarify that an entity recognizes revenue to depict the transfer of promised goods or services to customers in an amount that reflects the consideration to which the entity expects to be entitled in exchange for those goods or services.&nbsp;&nbsp;The amendments are effective for public business entities for annual reporting periods beginning after December 15, 2016, including interim periods within that reporting period.&nbsp;&nbsp;Early application is not permitted.&nbsp;&nbsp;The adoption of this ASU is not expected to have a material impact on the Company&#x2019;s consolidated financial statements.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">In June 2014, the FASB issued ASU No. 2014-11, </font><font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">Repurchase-to-Maturity Transactions, Repurchase Financings, and Disclosures.&nbsp; </font><font style="display: inline;">The amendments in this update require that repurchase-to-maturity transactions be accounted for as secured borrowings consistent with the accounting for other repurchase agreements.&nbsp;&nbsp;In addition, the amendments require separate accounting for a transfer of a financial asset executed contemporaneously with a repurchase agreement with the same counterparty (a repurchase financing), which will result in secured borrowing accounting for the repurchase agreement.&nbsp;&nbsp;The amendments require an entity to disclose information about transfers accounted for as sales in transactions that are economically similar to repurchase agreements, in which the transferor retains substantially all of the exposure to the economic return on the transferred financial asset throughout the term of the transaction.&nbsp;&nbsp;In addition, the amendments require disclosure of the types of collateral pledged in repurchase agreements, securities lending transactions, and repurchase-to-maturity transactions and the tenor of those transactions.&nbsp;&nbsp;The amendments are effective for public business entities for the first interim or annual period beginning after December 15, 2014, and for all other entities, the accounting changes are effective for annual periods beginning after December 15, 2014, and interim periods beginning after December 15, 2015.&nbsp;&nbsp;The adoption of this ASU is not expected to have a material impact on the Company&#x2019;s consolidated financial statements.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">

		</p>

		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">In June 2014, the FASB issued ASU No., 2014-12, </font><font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">Compensation- Stock Compensation (Topic 718):&nbsp;&nbsp;Accounting for Share-Based Payments When the Terms of an Award Provide That a Performance Target Could Be Achieved after the Requisite Service Period.&nbsp; </font><font style="display: inline;">The amendments in this update require that a performance target that affects vesting and that could be achieved after the requisite service period be treated as a performance condition.&nbsp;&nbsp;The amendments apply to reporting entities that grant their employees share-based payments in which the terms of the award provide that a performance target can be achieved after the requisite service period.&nbsp;&nbsp;For all entities, the amendments in this update are effective for annual periods and interim periods within those annual periods beginning after December 15, 2015.&nbsp;&nbsp;Early adoption is permitted.&nbsp;&nbsp;The adoption of this ASU is not expected to have a material impact on the Company&#x2019;s consolidated financial statements.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;color:#000000;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">

			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;color:#000000;font-size:12pt;">&nbsp;</font>

		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 10pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;;font-size: 12pt"><font style="display: inline;">Real Estate &#x2013; Residential &#x2013; This portfolio primarily consists of investor loans secured by properties in the Bank&#x2019;s normal lending area.&nbsp;&nbsp;Those investor loans are typically </font><font style="display: inline;">five</font><font style="display: inline;"> year rate adjustment loans.&nbsp;&nbsp;These loans generally have an original loan-to-va</font><font style="display: inline;">lue (LTV</font><font style="display: inline;">) of </font><font style="display: inline;">80</font><font style="display: inline;">% or less.&nbsp;&nbsp;This category also include</font><font style="display: inline;">s home equity lines of credit (HELOC</font><font style="display: inline;">).&nbsp;&nbsp;The HELOCs generally have an adjustable rate tied to prime rate and a term of </font><font style="display: inline;">10</font><font style="display: inline;"> years.&nbsp;&nbsp;Multifamily residential real estate is moderately seasoned and is generally secured by properties in the Bank&#x2019;s normal lending area. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 10pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Real Estate &#x2013; Commercial &#x2013; This portfolio consists of nonresidential improved real estate </font><font style="display: inline;">such as shopping centers and office buildings</font><font style="display: inline;">.&nbsp;&nbsp;These properties are generally located in the Bank&#x2019;s normal lending area.&nbsp; </font><font style="display: inline;">T</font><font style="display: inline;">his category of loans has a higher than average level of risk</font><font style="display: inline;"> because its performance is impacted by market forces over a longer time horizon</font><font style="display: inline;">. &nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 10pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Real Estate &#x2013; Residential Construction &#x2013;</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">These loans are located in the Bank&#x2019;s normal lending area. </font><font style="display: inline;"> While it has represented a growth area for the portfolio, this category also has a higher level of risk due to inherent market change and construction risks.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 10pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Real Estate &#x2013; Other Construction, Land Development and Other Land Loans &#x2013; This portfolio includes developed residential and commercial lots held by developers</font><font style="display: inline;"> as well as non-residential construction projects</font><font style="display: inline;">.&nbsp; </font><font style="display: inline;">This category has a higher level of risk due to inherent risks associated with market changes and construction.</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 10pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Commercial &#x2013; These loans include loans to businesses that are not secured by real estate.&nbsp;&nbsp;These loans are typically secured by accounts receivable, inventory, equipment, etc.&nbsp;&nbsp;Commercial loans are typically granted to local businesses that have a strong track record of profitability and performance. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 10pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Consumer &#x2013; Loans in this portfolio are either unsecured or secured by automobiles, marketable securities, etc.&nbsp;&nbsp;They are generally granted to local customers that have</font><font style="display: inline;"> a banking relationship with the</font><font style="display: inline;"> Bank. </font>
		</p>

				<td valign="bottom" style="width:10.56%;border-top:1pt solid #000000 ;border-left:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:2pt double #000000 ;border-right:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;background-color: #auto;height:15.00pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;text-align:right;" nowrap="nowrap"><div style="float:left"></div>431,340&nbsp;
				</td>

		</table></div>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 10pt;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Loans are determined past due or delinquent based on the contractual terms of the loan.&nbsp;&nbsp;Payments past due </font><font style="display: inline;">30</font><font style="display: inline;"> days or more are considered delinquent.&nbsp;&nbsp;The accrual of interest is generally discontinued at the time the loan is </font><font style="display: inline;">90</font><font style="display: inline;"> days delinquent unless the credit is well-secured and in process of collection.&nbsp;&nbsp;In all cases, loans are placed on nonaccrual at an earlier date if collection of principal or interest is considered doubtful or charged-off if a loss is considered imminent. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 10pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">All interest accrued but not collected for loans that are placed on nonaccrual </font><font style="display: inline;">is</font><font style="display: inline;"> reversed against interest income when the loan is placed on nonaccrual status.&nbsp;&nbsp;Because of the uncertainty of the expected cash flows, the Company is accounting for nonaccrual loans under the cost recovery method, in which all cash payments are applied to principal.&nbsp;&nbsp;Loans are returned to accrual status when all the principal and interest amounts contractually due are brought current and future collection of principal and interest are reasonably assured.&nbsp;&nbsp;The number of payments needed to meet this criteria varies from loan to loan.&nbsp;&nbsp;However, as a general rule, this criteria will be considered to have been met with the timely payment of </font><font style="display: inline;">six</font><font style="display: inline;"> consecutive regularly scheduled monthly payments. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 10pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">

		</p>

		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 10pt;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">These credit quality indicators are defined as follows: </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 10pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Pass &#x2013; A &#x201C;pass&#x201D; rated loan</font><font style="display: inline;"> is not adversely classified because it does not display any of the characteristics for adverse classification. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 10pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Special</font><font style="display: inline;"> Mention &#x2013; A &#x201C;special mention&#x201D; loan</font><font style="display: inline;"> has potential weaknesses that deserve management&#x2019;s close attention. If left uncorrected, such potential weaknesses may result in deterioration of the repayment prospects or collateral position at some future date. Special mention assets do not warrant adverse classification. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 10pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Sub</font><font style="display: inline;">standard &#x2013; A &#x201C;substandard&#x201D; loan</font><font style="display: inline;"> is inadequately protected by the current net worth and paying capacity of the obligor or of the collateral pledged, if any. Assets classified as substandard generally have a well-defined weakness, or weaknesses, that jeopardize the liquidation of the debt. These assets are characterized by the distinct possibility of loss if the deficiencies are not corrected. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 10pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Doubtful &#x2013; A</font><font style="display: inline;"> loan</font><font style="display: inline;"> classified &#x201C;doubtful&#x201D; has all the weaknesses inherent in an asset classified substandard with the added characteristic that the weaknesses make collection or liquidation in full highly questionable and improbable, on the basis of currently existing facts, conditions, and values. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 10pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Loss &#x2013; Assets classified &#x201C;loss&#x201D; are considered uncollectible and of such little value that their continuing to be carried as an asset is not warranted. This classification is not necessarily equivalent to no potential for recovery or salvage value, but rather that it is not appropriate to defer a full write-off even though partial recovery may be effected in the future. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 10pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The loan risk rankings were updated for the year ended December 31, 201</font><font style="display: inline;">4,</font><font style="display: inline;"> on Decembe</font><font style="display: inline;">r &nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">16</font><font style="display: inline;"> and 1</font><font style="display: inline;">7</font><font style="display: inline;">, 201</font><font style="display: inline;">4</font><font style="display: inline;">.</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">The loan risk</font><font style="display: inline;"> rankings were updated for the year</font><font style="display: inline;"> ended </font><font style="display: inline;">December 31, 2013,</font><font style="display: inline;"> on </font><font style="display: inline;">December 10 and 11, 2013</font><font style="display: inline;">.&nbsp; </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 10pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The following table provides details regarding impaired loans by segment and class at </font><font style="display: inline;">December 31</font><font style="display: inline;">, 201</font><font style="display: inline;">4,</font><font style="display: inline;"> and December 31, 201</font><font style="display: inline;">3</font><font style="display: inline;">: &nbsp;</font>
		</p>

			<font style="display: inline;">A loan is considered impaired when, based on current information and events, it is probable that the Company will be unable to collect the scheduled payments on principal and interest when due according to the contractual terms of the loan agreement.&nbsp;&nbsp;Factors considered by management in determining whether a loan is impaired include payment status, collateral value, and the probability of collecting scheduled principal and interest payments when due.&nbsp;&nbsp;Additionally, management&#x2019;s policy is generally to evaluate only those </font><font style="display: inline;">substandard </font><font style="display: inline;">loans greater than $</font><font style="display: inline;">250</font><font style="display: inline;"> thousand for impairment as these are considered to be individually significant in relation to the size of the loan portfolio.&nbsp;&nbsp;Management determines the significance of payment delays and payment shortfalls on a case-by-case basis, taking into consideration all of the circumstances surrounding the loan and the borrower, including the length of delay, the reasons for the delay, the borrower&#x2019;s prior payment record, and the amount of the shortfall in relation to the principal and interest owed.&nbsp;&nbsp;Impairment is measured on a loan-by-loan basis by either the present value of expected future cash flows discounted at the loan&#x2019;s effective interest rate, the loan&#x2019;s obtainable market price, or the fair value of the collateral if the loan is collateral dependent.&nbsp;&nbsp;The following table</font><font style="display: inline;">s</font><font style="display: inline;"> present interest income recognized and the average recorded investment of impaired loans</font><font style="display: inline;">:</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>

			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 10pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Cash payments received on impaired loans are applied on a cash basis with all cash receipts applied first to principal and any payments received in excess of the unpaid principal balance being applied to interest. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 10pt;font-weight:bold;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Troubled Debt Restructurings</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 10pt;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Accounting Standards Codification (ASC) 310 defines a troubled-debt restructuring as a restructuring of debt where a creditor for economic or legal reasons related to a debtor&#x2019;s financial difficulties grants a concession to the debtor that it would not otherwise render.&nbsp;&nbsp;The concession is granted by the creditor in an attempt to protect as much of its investment as possible.&nbsp;&nbsp;The concession either stems from an agreement between the creditor and the debtor or is imposed by law or a court.&nbsp;&nbsp;Troubled-debt restructurings include modification of the terms of a debt, such as a reduction of the stated interest rate lower than the current market for new debt with similar risk, a reduction of the face amount or maturity amount of the debt as stated in the instrument or other agreement, or a reduction of accrued interest.&nbsp; </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 10pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Management reviews all restructured loans that occur during the year for identification as troubled-debt restructurings.&nbsp;&nbsp;Management iden</font><font style="display: inline;">tified as troubled-debt restructurings certain loans for which the allowance for loan losses had previously been measured under a general allowance for loan losses methodology (ASC 450).&nbsp;&nbsp;Upon identifying the reviewed loans as troubled-debt restructurings, management also identified them as impaired under the guidance in ASC 310.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 10pt;font-weight:bold;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Modification Categories</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 10pt;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The Company offers a variety of modifications to borrowers. The modification categories offered can generally be described </font><font style="display: inline;">as follows</font><font style="display: inline;">: &nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 10pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Rate Modification - A modification in which the interest rate is changed. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 10pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Term Modification - A modification in which the maturity date, timing of payments, or frequency of payments is changed. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 10pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Interest Only Modification &#x2013; A modification in which the loan is converted to interest only payments for a period of time. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 10pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">

		</p>
		<p><font size="1"> </font></p><div style="width:100%">

		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:center;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 11pt">

			<font style="display: inline;">F-</font><font style="display: inline;">26</font>

		</p>

		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 11pt">

			&nbsp;

		</p>

</div><hr size="3" style="color:#999999" width="100%" align="center"></hr><p style="page-break-after:always">&nbsp;</p><div style="width:100%">

		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 11pt">

			&nbsp;

		</p>

</div>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 10pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;;font-size: 12pt"><font style="display: inline;">Payment Modification &#x2013; A modification in which the dollar amount of the payment is changed, other than an interest only modification described above. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 10pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Combination Modification &#x2013; Any other type of modification, including the use of multiple categories above. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 10pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">

		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 10pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">

		<p style="margin:0pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;color:#000000;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;color:#000000;font-size:12pt;">Note 8 &#x2013; Subordinated Debt</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;color:#000000;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;font-size:12pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:12pt;">In </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:12pt;">December 2005</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:12pt;">, $</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:12pt;">2.0</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:12pt;"> million of subordinated debt was issued by the Bank through a pooled underwriting.&nbsp;&nbsp;The securities had a fixed rate for </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:12pt;">five</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:12pt;"> years then converted to three-month LIBOR plus </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:12pt;">1.37</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:12pt;">% in December 2010 and is payable quarterly.&nbsp;&nbsp;The securities may be redeemed at par beginning December 2010 and each quarter after such date until the securities mature on December 31, 2015.&nbsp;&nbsp;The interest rate at December 31, 2013 was </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:12pt;">1.61</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:12pt;">%, and the balance outstanding at December 31, 2013 was $</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:12pt;">2.0</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:12pt;"> million.&nbsp;&nbsp;During 2014, the Company redeemed these securities. As such, there is </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:12pt;">no</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:12pt;"> remaining balance related to these securities at December 31, 2014.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:12pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:12pt;">In January 2014, the Company executed a variable rate subordinated note for </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:12pt;">$6.5</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:12pt;"> million with a financial institution.&nbsp;&nbsp;The note carries an interest rate of 30-day LIBOR plus </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:12pt;">5.00%</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:12pt;"> per annum with a floor of </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:12pt;">5.50%</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:12pt;"> and a maturity of </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:12pt;">10</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:12pt;"> years.&nbsp;&nbsp;Principal is repaid </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:12pt;">$8</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:12pt;"> thousand per month for the first 60 months then </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:12pt;">$100</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:12pt;"> thousand per month for the remaining 60 months.&nbsp;&nbsp;The interest rate at December 31, 2014 was </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:12pt;">5.50%</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:12pt;">, and the balance outstanding was </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:12pt;">$6.4</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:12pt;"> million.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:12pt;">&nbsp;</font>

		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 10pt;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;;font-size: 12pt"><font style="display: inline;">Note 16</font><font style="display: inline;"> &#x2013; Fair Value Disclosures</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 10pt;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The Company uses fair value measurements to record fair value adjustments to certain assets and liabilities and to determine fair value disclosures.&nbsp;&nbsp;In accordance with the Fair Valu</font><font style="display: inline;">e Measurements and Disclosures (T</font><font style="display: inline;">opic ASC</font><font style="display: inline;"> 820)</font><font style="display: inline;">, the fair value of a financial instrument is the price that would be received in the sale of an asset or paid to transfer the liability in an orderly transaction between market participants at the measurement date.&nbsp;&nbsp;Fair value is best determined </font><font style="display: inline;">using</font><font style="display: inline;"> quoted market prices.&nbsp;&nbsp;However, in many instances, there are no quoted market prices for the Company&#x2019;s various financial instruments.&nbsp;&nbsp;In cases where quoted market prices are not available, fair values are based on estimates using present value or other valuation techniques.&nbsp;&nbsp;Those techniques are significantly affected by the assumptions used, including the discount rate and estimates of future cash flows.&nbsp;&nbsp;Accordingly, the fair value estimates may not be realized in an immediate settlement of the instrument. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 10pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The recent fair value guidance provides a consistent definition of fair value, which focuses on exit price in an orderly transaction (that is, not a forced liquidation or distressed sale) between market participants at the measurement date under current market conditions.&nbsp;&nbsp;If there has been a significant decrease in the volume and level of activity for the asset or liability, a change in valuation technique or the use of multiple valuation techniques may be appropriate.&nbsp;&nbsp;In such instances, determining the price at which willing market participants would transact </font><font style="display: inline;">on</font><font style="display: inline;"> the measurement date under current market conditions depends on the facts and circumstances and requires the use of significant judgment. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 10pt;font-weight:bold;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Fair Value </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 10pt;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">In accordance with this guidance, </font><font style="display: inline;">the Company groups</font><font style="display: inline;"> financial assets and financial liabilities generally measured at fair value in three levels, based on the markets in which the assets and liabilities are traded and the reliability of the assumptions used to determine the fair value. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 10pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Level 1 &#x2013; Valuation is based on quoted prices in active markets for identical assets or liabilities in active markets at the measurement date.&nbsp;&nbsp;Level 1 assets and liabilities generally include debt and equity securities that are traded in an active exchange market.&nbsp;&nbsp;Valuations are obtained from readily available pricing sources for market transactions involving identical assets or liabilities. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 10pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Level 2 &#x2013; Valuation is based on inputs other than quoted prices included within level 1 that are observable for the asset or liability, either directly or indirectly.&nbsp;&nbsp;The valuation may be based on quoted prices for similar assets or liabilities; quoted prices in markets that are not active; or other inputs that are observable or can be corroborated by observable market date for substantially the full term of the asset or liability. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 10pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Level 3 &#x2013; Valuation is based on unobservable inputs that are supported by little or no market activity and that are significant to the fair value of the assets or liabilities.&nbsp;&nbsp;Level 3 assets and liabilities include financial instruments whose value is determined using pricing models, discounted cash flows methodologies, or similar techniques, as well as instruments for which determination of fair value requires significant management judgment or estimation. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 10pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">

		</p>
		<p><font size="1"> </font></p><div style="width:100%">

		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:center;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 11pt">

			<font style="display: inline;">F-</font><font style="display: inline;">38</font>

		</p>

		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 11pt">

			&nbsp;

		</p>

</div><hr size="3" style="color:#999999" width="100%" align="center"></hr><p style="page-break-after:always">&nbsp;</p><div style="width:100%">

		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 11pt">

			&nbsp;

		</p>

		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 10pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;;font-size: 12pt"><font style="display: inline;">Following is a description of the valuation methodologies used for instruments measured as fair value, as well as the general classification of such instruments pursuant to the valuation hierarchy: </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 10pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">Securities available for sale</font><font style="display: inline;">:&nbsp;&nbsp;Securities available for sale are recorded at fair value on a recurring basis.&nbsp;&nbsp;Fair value measurement is based upon quoted market prices, when available (Level 1).&nbsp;&nbsp;If quoted market prices are not available, fair values are measured utilizing independent valuation techniques of identical or similar securities for which significant assumptions are derived primarily from or corroborated by observable market data.&nbsp;&nbsp;Third party vendors compile prices from various sources and may determine the fair value of identical or similar securities by using pricing models that consider observable market data (Level 2).&nbsp; </font><font style="display: inline;">The Company obtains</font><font style="display: inline;"> a single quote for all se</font><font style="display: inline;">curities.&nbsp;&nbsp;Quotes for all </font><font style="display: inline;">securities are provided by </font><font style="display: inline;">the Company&#x2019;s</font><font style="display: inline;"> securities accounting and safekeeping correspondent bank.&nbsp; </font><font style="display: inline;">The Company</font><font style="display: inline;"> perform</font><font style="display: inline;">s</font><font style="display: inline;"> a review of pricing data by comparing prices received from third party vendors to the previous month&#x2019;s quote for the same security and evaluate any substantial changes. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 10pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The following tables present the balances of financial assets and liabilities measured at fair value on a recurring basis as of</font><font style="display: inline;"> December 31, 2014, and</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">December 31, 2013</font><font style="display: inline;">. Securities identified in Note 3 as restricted securities including stock in the F</font><font style="display: inline;">HLB</font><font style="display: inline;"> and the Federal Reserve Bank</font><font style="display: inline;"> (FRB</font><font style="display: inline;">)</font><font style="display: inline;"> are excluded from the table below since there is no ability to sell these securities except when the FHLB or FRB require redemption based on either </font><font style="display: inline;">the Company&#x2019;s </font><font style="display: inline;">borrowings at the FHLB, or in the case of the FRB</font><font style="display: inline;">,</font><font style="display: inline;"> changes in certain portions of </font><font style="display: inline;">the Company&#x2019;s </font><font style="display: inline;">capital. </font>

			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>

		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 10pt;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Certain assets are measured at fair value on a nonrecurring basis in accordance with GAAP.&nbsp;&nbsp;Adjustments to the fair value of these assets usually result from the application of lower-of-cost-or-market accounting or write-downs of individual loans. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 10pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">

		<p><font size="1"> </font></p><div style="width:100%">

		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:center;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 11pt">

			<font style="display: inline;">F-</font><font style="display: inline;">39</font>

		</p>

		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 11pt">

			&nbsp;

</div><hr size="3" style="color:#999999" width="100%" align="center"></hr><p style="page-break-after:always">&nbsp;</p><div style="width:100%">

		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 11pt">

			&nbsp;

		</p>

</div>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 10pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;;font-size: 12pt"><font style="display: inline;">The following describes the valuation techniques used to measure certain assets recorded at fair value on a nonrecurring basis in the </font><font style="display: inline;">accompanying consolidated </font><font style="display: inline;">financial statements. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 10pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">Impaired Loans</font><font style="display: inline;">:&nbsp;&nbsp;Loans are designated as impaired when, in the judgment of management, based on current information and events, it is probable that all amounts when due according to the contractual terms of the loan agreement will not be collected.&nbsp;&nbsp;The measurement of loss associated with impaired loans can be based on either the observable market price of the loan or the fair value of the collateral.&nbsp;&nbsp;Fair value is measured based on the value of the collateral securing the loans.&nbsp;&nbsp;Collateral may be in the form of real estate or business assets including equipment, inventory, and accounts receivable.&nbsp;&nbsp;The vast majority of the collateral is real estate.&nbsp; </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 10pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The value of real estate co</font><font style="display: inline;">llateral is determined utilizing</font><font style="display: inline;"> an income or market valuation approach based on an appraisal conducted by an independent, licensed external appraiser using observable market dat</font><font style="display: inline;">a</font><font style="display: inline;"> (Level </font><font style="display: inline;">2</font><font style="display: inline;">).&nbsp;&nbsp;However, if the collateral is a house or building in the process of construction or if an appraisal of the real estate property is over </font><font style="display: inline;">two</font><font style="display: inline;"> years old</font><font style="display: inline;"> or management determines the fair value of the collateral is further impaired below the appraised value and there is no observable market price</font><font style="display: inline;">, then the fair value is considered Level 3.&nbsp;&nbsp;If a real estate loan becomes a nonperforming loan, or if the valuation is over </font><font style="display: inline;">one</font><font style="display: inline;"> year old, either an evaluation by an officer of the bank or an outside vendor, or an appraisal is performed to determine current market value.&nbsp; </font><font style="display: inline;">The Company considers</font><font style="display: inline;"> the value of a par</font><font style="display: inline;">tially completed project for its</font><font style="display: inline;"> loan analysis.&nbsp;&nbsp;For nonperforming construction loans, </font><font style="display: inline;">the Company obtains</font><font style="display: inline;"> a valuation of each par</font><font style="display: inline;">tially completed project &#x201C;as is&#x201D;</font><font style="display: inline;"> from a third party appraiser.&nbsp; </font><font style="display: inline;">The Company uses</font><font style="display: inline;"> this third party valuation to determine if any charge-offs are necessary. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 10pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The value of business equipment </font><font style="display: inline;">collateral </font><font style="display: inline;">is based upon an outside appraisal if deemed significant, or the net book value on the applicable business&#x2019; financial statements if not considered significant using observable market data.&nbsp;&nbsp;Likewise, values for inventory and accounts receivable collateral are based on </font><font style="display: inline;">the related </font><font style="display: inline;">financial statement balances or aging reports (Level 3).&nbsp; </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 10pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">I</font><font style="display: inline;">mpaired loans allocated to the allowance for loan l</font><font style="display: inline;">osses are measured at fair value on</font><font style="display: inline;"> a nonrecurring basis with a</font><font style="display: inline;"> discount to reflect current market conditions</font><font style="display: inline;">, which</font><font style="display: inline;"> ranged from </font><font style="display: inline;">0</font><font style="display: inline;">% to </font><font style="display: inline;">30</font><font style="display: inline;">%, for each of the</font><font style="display: inline;"> periods</font><font style="display: inline;"> presented</font><font style="display: inline;">.&nbsp;&nbsp;Any fair value adjustments are recorded in the period incurre</font><font style="display: inline;">d as provision for loan losses i</font><font style="display: inline;">n the </font><font style="display: inline;">accompanying </font><font style="display: inline;">Consolidated Statements of Operations. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 10pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">Loans held for sale:&nbsp; </font><font style="display: inline;">The fair value of loans held for sale is determined using quoted secondary-market prices.&nbsp;&nbsp;As such, </font><font style="display: inline;">the Company classifies</font><font style="display: inline;"> loans subjected to nonrecurring fair value adjustments as Level 2. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">Other Real Estate Owned</font><font style="display: inline;">:&nbsp; </font><font style="display: inline;">Assets acquired through or instead of loan foreclosure are initially recorded at fair value less costs to sell when acquired, establishing a new cost basis.&nbsp;&nbsp;These assets are subsequently accounted for at lower of cost or fair value less estimated costs to sell. Fair value is commonly based on recent real estate appraisals which are updated no less frequently than annually. These appraisals may utilize a single valuation approach or a combination of approaches including comparable sales and the income approach. Adjustments are routinely made in the appraisal process by the independent appraisers to adjust for differences between the comparable sales and income data available. Such adjustments are usually significant and typically result in a Level 3 classification of the inputs for determining fair value.</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:9pt;"> &nbsp; &nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">Real estate owned properties are evaluated on a quarterly basis for additional impairment and adjusted accordingly.&nbsp;&nbsp;Such appraisals may be discounted for current market conditions and ranged from 0% to 30% for each of the respective periods presented in the accompanying </font><font style="display: inline;">consolidated </font><font style="display: inline;">financial statements.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:9pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">

		</p>

		</p>

			<font style="display: inline;">The methods and assumptions</font><font style="display: inline;">, not previously presented,</font><font style="display: inline;"> used by the Company in estimating fair values a</font><font style="display: inline;">re</font><font style="display: inline;"> disclosed </font><font style="display: inline;">as follows</font><font style="display: inline;">: &nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 10pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">Cash and </font><font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">cash equivalents</font><font style="display: inline;"> &nbsp;&#x2013;</font><font style="display: inline;"> The carrying amounts of cash and </font><font style="display: inline;">cash equivalents</font><font style="display: inline;"> approximate their fair value. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 10pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">Loans receivable</font><font style="display: inline;"> &nbsp;&#x2013;</font><font style="display: inline;"> Fair values are based on carrying values for variable-rate loans that reprice frequently and have no significant change in credit risk.&nbsp;&nbsp;Fair values for certain mortgage loans (for example, one-to-four family residential) and other consumer loans are based on quoted market prices of similar loans sold in conjunction with securitization transactions, adjusted for differences in loan characteristics.&nbsp;&nbsp;Fair values for commercial real estate and commercial loans are estimated using discounted cash flow analyses and interest rates currently being offered for loans with similar terms to borrowers of similar credit quality.&nbsp;&nbsp;The interest rates on loans at</font><font style="display: inline;"> December 31, 2014, and</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">December 31, 2013</font><font style="display: inline;"> are current market rates for their respective terms and associated credit risk. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 10pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">Loans held for sale</font><font style="display: inline;">&#x2014;Loans held for sale are carried at the lower of cost or market value.&nbsp;&nbsp;These loans currently consist of residential real estate, owner occupied loans originated for sale in the secondary market.&nbsp;&nbsp;Fair value is based on the price secondary markets are currently offering for similar loans using observable market data which is not materially different from cost due to the short duration between origination and sale (Level 2).&nbsp;&nbsp;As such, the Company records any fair value adjustments on a nonrecurring basis.&nbsp; </font><font style="display: inline;">No</font><font style="display: inline;"> nonrecurring fair value adjustments were recorded on loans held for sale during the periods ended</font><font style="display: inline;"> December 31, 2014, and</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">December 31, 2013</font><font style="display: inline;">.&nbsp;&nbsp;Gains and losses on the sale of lo</font><font style="display: inline;">ans are recorded as income i</font><font style="display: inline;">n the </font><font style="display: inline;">accompanying consolidated statements of o</font><font style="display: inline;">perations. </font>
		</p>

		</p>

		</p>

		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 10pt;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;;font-size: 12pt"><font style="display: inline;">The Company assumes</font><font style="display: inline;"> interest rate risk (the risk that general interest rate levels will change) as a result of</font><font style="display: inline;"> its</font><font style="display: inline;"> normal operations.&nbsp;&nbsp;As a result, the fair values of financial instruments will change when interest rates levels change</font><font style="display: inline;">,</font><font style="display: inline;"> and that change may be eith</font><font style="display: inline;">er favorable or unfavorable</font><font style="display: inline;">.&nbsp; </font><font style="display: inline;">The Company attempts</font><font style="display: inline;"> to match maturities of assets and liabilities to the extent believed necessary to minimize interest rate risk.&nbsp;&nbsp;However, borrowers with fixed rate obligations are less likely to repay in a rising rate environment.&nbsp;&nbsp;Conversely, depositors who are receiving fixed rates are more likely to withdraw funds before maturity in a rising rate environment and less likely to do so in a falling rate environment.&nbsp; </font><font style="display: inline;">The Company monitors</font><font style="display: inline;"> rates and maturities of assets and liabilities and attempt</font><font style="display: inline;">s</font><font style="display: inline;"> to minimize interest rate risk by adjusting terms of new loans and deposits and by investing in securit</font><font style="display: inline;">ies with terms that mitigate</font><font style="display: inline;"> overall interest rate risk.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 10pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">

			<font style="display: inline;font-size:12pt;">The Company has a First Capital Bancorp, Inc. 2000 Stock Option Plan (the Plan) pursuant to which options may be granted to Directors, officers and key employees.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Plan authorizes grants of options to purchase up to </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:12pt;">338,484</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:12pt;"> shares of the Company&#x2019;s authorized, but unissued common stock.&nbsp;&nbsp;All stock options have been granted with an exercise price equal to the stock&#x2019;s fair market value at the date of grant.&nbsp;&nbsp;Stock options generally have </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:12pt;">10</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:12pt;">-year terms and vest at the rate of </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:12pt;">50</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:12pt;"> percent per year for Directors or </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:12pt;">33</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:12pt;"> 1/3 percent per year for employees.</font>

		</p>

			<font style="display: inline;">During 2012, the Company raised approximately $</font><font style="display: inline;">17.8</font><font style="display: inline;"> million, net of fees and costs, through a rights offering.&nbsp;&nbsp;In connection with the rights offering, the Company distributed </font><font style="display: inline;">8.9</font><font style="display: inline;"> million warrants to purchase </font><font style="display: inline;">one</font><font style="display: inline;">-half of a share of common stock for $</font><font style="display: inline;">2.00</font><font style="display: inline;"> per whole share.</font><font style="display: inline;"> &nbsp;During the years ended December 31, 2014 and 2013, </font><font style="display: inline;">430</font><font style="display: inline;"> thousand and </font><font style="display: inline;">708</font><font style="display: inline;"> thousand warrants, respectively, were exercised leaving </font><font style="display: inline;">7.7</font><font style="display: inline;"> million and </font><font style="display: inline;">8.1</font><font style="display: inline;"> million warrants outstanding at December 31, 2014 and 2013, respectively.</font>

			<font style="display: inline;">As described in Note 17, t</font><font style="display: inline;">he 2010 Plan permits the granting of non-vested restricted stock.&nbsp;&nbsp;The grants are divided between restricted time-based stock grants and restricted performance&#x2013;based stock grants.&nbsp;&nbsp;Generally, the restricted time-based grants vest </font><font style="display: inline;">33</font><font style="display: inline;">% per year for employees and </font><font style="display: inline;">50</font><font style="display: inline;">% per year for Directors.&nbsp;&nbsp;The restricted performance-based stock is subject to vesting on the third anniversary of the date of the grant based on the performance of the Company&#x2019;s growth in cumulative tangible book value and cumulative fully-diluted earnings per share growth over a </font><font style="display: inline;">three</font><font style="display: inline;">-year period.&nbsp;&nbsp;In December 2013, the board of directors approved the acceleration of vesting for both the time and performance based stock for the CEO such that those shares awarded became fully vested at December 31, 2013. The accelerated vesting of these </font><font style="display: inline;">100,000</font><font style="display: inline;"> shares in 2013 resulted in </font><font style="display: inline;">additional </font><font style="display: inline;">compensation expense of </font><font style="display: inline;">$206</font><font style="display: inline;"> thousand.&nbsp;&nbsp;The value of the non-vested stock awards was calculated by multiplying the fair value of the Company&#x2019;s common stock on grant date by the number of shares awarded.&nbsp;&nbsp;Recipients of the awards have the right to vote the shares and to receive cash or stock dividends, if any.</font>
